Overview

Cologne as a Business Centre

Cologne had 1,087,353 residents at the end of 2023, according to the Cologne Chamber of Industry and Commerce (IHK Köln), and generated gross domestic product of about EUR 66.7 billion in 2021. The city counted roughly 632,000 employees subject to social security at workplaces in Cologne in 2025, the large majority in services. More than fifty German insurers and reinsurers are headquartered there, making it the country's second-largest insurance location. Information and communication, health care, wholesale and retail, manufacturing and transport are all significant employers. Cologne/Bonn Airport handled about 10 million passengers and 842,000 tonnes of air cargo in 2025, and the Rhine ports remain part of the regional freight network.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Cologne because claims, contracts and corporate control in several of Germany's largest service sectors run through the city. Insurers and reinsurers need claims and intermediary investigations; acquirers and lenders need to understand mid-sized family companies, media and production businesses and logistics operators in the Rhineland; litigators need background on parties and witnesses before the Cologne courts. Cologne also recorded 450 company insolvencies in 2025, which brings creditor and asset-tracing questions. Because the commercial register for the Cologne region is kept by the local court and German privacy law is strict, the work must be scoped carefully from the outset.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Cologne

01

Insurance claims and intermediary investigations

With dozens of insurers and reinsurers headquartered in Cologne, claims questions arise across property, liability, motor and commercial lines. We support claims and legal teams with lawful background, corporate and asset research on claimants, brokers and service providers, coordinating German professionals for any local inquiries.

02

Media and production counterparty diligence

Information and communication is a major employer in Cologne. Before co-productions, licensing deals or acquisitions, we review the ownership, register filings, litigation and reputational record of production companies and their principals, so clients understand who controls a partner and what history they bring.

03

Family company and Mittelstand acquisitions

Many Rhineland businesses are privately held through GmbH and partnership structures. We trace shareholdings, managing directors and related entities through the Cologne commercial register and published accounts, and examine litigation and insolvency history to support acquirers, investors and lenders.

04

Logistics and airfreight partner checks

Cologne/Bonn Airport is a major air cargo hub and the region supports road, rail and inland waterway freight. We examine forwarders, carriers and warehouse operators for ownership, related parties, insolvency signals and adverse media before contracts are signed or cargo exposure grows.

05

Insolvency and creditor asset research

Cologne recorded 450 company insolvencies in 2025. We assist creditors, administrators' counsel and investors in identifying related companies, transfers of assets before insolvency and the subsequent business activities of former managing directors, using register, insolvency publication and court sources.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Cologne

Courts sitting in Cologne

The Higher Regional Court of Cologne (Oberlandesgericht Köln), at Reichenspergerplatz 1, is one of three higher regional courts in North Rhine-Westphalia and hears appeals in civil and commercial matters from its district. Below it, the Cologne Regional Court (Landgericht Köln) hears larger commercial and civil claims at first instance, including through chambers for commercial matters. Counsel decides forum and procedure; our research is scoped to what the court will need.

Commercial register at Cologne Local Court

The Cologne Local Court (Amtsgericht Köln) keeps the commercial and cooperative register for a district covering Cologne, Leverkusen, the Rhein-Erft and Rheinisch-Bergisch districts and part of the Oberbergischer Kreis, including the local court districts of Bergheim, Bergisch Gladbach, Brühl, Gummersbach, Kerpen, Wermelskirchen and Wipperfürth. Entries and filed documents are accessed through the national register portal described on our Germany page.

IHK Köln chamber of commerce

The Cologne Chamber of Industry and Commerce, founded in 1797, is a public-law body whose membership includes nearly all commercially active businesses in Cologne, Leverkusen and the Oberberg, Rhein-Berg and Rhein-Erft districts, about 150,000 companies. It advises on location and legal issues, liaises with authorities and courts, and runs vocational training. Its statistical publications are a useful reference for the regional economy. It also maintains links with chambers abroad.

North Rhine-Westphalia framework

Cologne sits in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany's most populous state, which administers the state courts and the state data protection authority. Federal rules govern detective businesses, which register a trade and are subject to supervision as described on our Germany page; there is no separate Cologne licence. Any local inquiries are coordinated with appropriately registered German professionals and counsel. Proceedings before the Cologne courts are conducted in German.

Questions

Cologne: Frequently Asked Questions

Which court keeps the commercial register for Cologne companies?

The Cologne Local Court (Amtsgericht Köln) keeps the commercial and cooperative register for Cologne, Leverkusen, the Rhein-Erft and Rheinisch-Bergisch districts and part of the Oberbergischer Kreis. Its entries and filed documents can be consulted through Germany's joint register portal, so we usually begin research there before turning to accounts and court sources.

Can you support insurers headquartered in Cologne?

Yes. Cologne is Germany's second-largest insurance location, and we support claims and legal teams with background, corporate and asset research on claimants, intermediaries and suppliers, including parties outside Germany. We work within GDPR and German law, documenting the legitimate interest, and coordinate German professionals for any local inquiries.

Where are commercial disputes heard in Cologne?

Larger civil and commercial claims are generally heard at first instance by the Cologne Regional Court, with appeals to the Higher Regional Court of Cologne. Counsel determines forum and strategy; we tailor research on parties, witnesses and corporate histories to the procedural needs of the case.

Do investigators need a special licence in Cologne?

There is no Cologne-specific licence. Under federal trade law, detective businesses in Germany register a trade and are subject to reliability supervision rather than a dedicated licensing regime. TDSC does not conduct local fieldwork itself and coordinates appropriately registered German professionals, with counsel confirming the rules for each assignment.

Can you trace assets after a Cologne company becomes insolvent?

We research related companies, shareholdings, real estate indications and the later activities of former managing directors using register entries, insolvency publications, court decisions and media. Findings are presented with sources so the client's German counsel or the administrator can decide what legal steps are appropriate.
